Rule of Three Calculator

Find a missing value from three known ones. Use direct proportion when both go up together, inverse when one goes up as the other goes down.

Direct Proportion

More of one means more of the other. If A gives B, how much does C give? Example: 2 kg cost $300, so 5 kg cost $750.

=

Inverse Proportion

More of one means less of the other. If A workers need B days, how many days do C workers need? Example: 4 workers take 10 days, so 8 workers take 5 days.

=

How the Rule of Three Works

Write the two pairs as a ratio: A is to B as C is to X. For direct proportion, X = B × C ÷ A. For inverse proportion, X = A × B ÷ C.

Everyday examples: a recipe for 4 people scaled to 6, the price of 750 grams when you know the price per kilo, how long a trip takes at a different speed, or how many days a job needs with more workers.

Questions & Answers

What is the rule of three?

The rule of three finds a missing fourth value when three values are known and two quantities are in proportion. It is used every day for prices, recipes, fuel, exchange rates and dosages.

What is the formula for the direct rule of three?

If A corresponds to B, then C corresponds to B × C ÷ A. Example: 2 kg cost $300, so 5 kg cost 300 × 5 ÷ 2 = $750.

When do I use the inverse rule of three?

Use it when one quantity goes up as the other goes down, such as workers and days, or speed and travel time. The formula is A × B ÷ C.

Is the rule of three the same as cross multiplication?

Yes. Both set up two equal ratios, A/B = C/X, and solve for the unknown X by multiplying across.
